paper_title: SepLLM Accelerate Large Language Models by Compressing One Segment into   One Separator
caption: : Loss Ratio FLOPs
model_annotation: The line plot illustrates the loss ratio (%) as a function of total floating-point operations (TFLOPs) for five different configurations: Vanilla, SepLLM (n=64), SepLLM (n=128), SepLLM (n=64, H), and SepLLM (n=64, H/T). The x-axis, labeled “TFLOPs,” spans from 1e7 to 9e8 on a logarithmic scale, with major tick marks at 1e7, 2e7, 5e7, 1e8, 2e8, 5e8, and 9e8. The y-axis, labeled “Loss Ratio (%)”, ranges from 94% to 100% on a linear scale, with tick marks at 94, 95, 96, 97, 98, 99, and 100. The “Vanilla” configuration (purple triangles, solid line) remains nearly flat near 100% across all TFLOPs. “SepLLM (n=64)” (orange squares, solid line) starts at ~98.3% at 1e7 TFLOPs, rises to ~100.1% at 4e8, then slightly declines to ~99.9% at 9e8. “SepLLM (n=128)” (blue crosses, solid line) begins at ~97.1% at 1e7, climbs to ~99.8% at 5e7, and stabilizes near 99.9% through 9e8. “SepLLM (n=64, H)” (green diamonds, solid line) starts at ~97.6% at 1e7, increases to ~100% at 5e7, and fluctuates slightly around 99.9–100% thereafter. “SepLLM (n=64, H/T)” (red circles, solid line) begins at 94% at 1e7, rises steeply to ~97.8% at 5e7, continues increasing to ~99.3% at 4e8, peaks at ~99.1% at 5e8, then gently declines to ~98.7% at 9e8.
